mark.label: Four linked relay segments circling a shared route

semanticColorUsage.background: The neutral route behind every working surface.
semanticColorUsage.foreground: Primary copy, strong labels, and high emphasis symbols.
semanticColorUsage.card: Focused working planes and bounded evidence regions.
semanticColorUsage.muted: Supporting bands, inactive stages, and secondary controls.
semanticColorUsage.mutedForeground: Context, timestamps, and secondary evidence that remain readable.
semanticColorUsage.border: Route boundaries, control outlines, and internal stage rules.
semanticColorUsage.primary: The active route, primary action, focus, links, and current selection.
semanticColorUsage.primaryForeground: Readable content placed on the primary cue.
semanticColorUsage.destructive: Irreversible actions, failed operations, and critical errors.
semanticColorUsage.success: Verified completion and healthy outcomes, distinct from active progress.
semanticColorUsage.warning: Attention that may delay progress without representing failure.
semanticColorUsage.info: Neutral instructions, queued state, and explanatory feedback.
semanticColorUsage.ring: Keyboard focus around every interactive control.

display.usage: Singular product outcomes and major chapter statements.

heading.usage: Page, section, and decision region hierarchy.

body.usage: Interface explanations, guidance, and readable product copy.

label.usage: Stage indices, compact metadata, counters, and wayfinding.

metric.usage: Progress totals and operational summaries with visible units.

code.usage: Identifiers, timestamps, commands, and technical values.

2.usage: Compact inline groups and status details.

5.usage: Process band padding and related control groups.

6.usage: Cards, panels, and distinct component sections.

8.usage: Major product groups and evidence separation.

12.usage: Chapter transitions and compact marketing sections.

16.usage: Major product and marketing composition breaks.

layout.guidance: Arrange sequential process bands on a stable route, alternate concise outcomes with evidence, and keep active work beside its context.

mobile.guidance: Stack stages in source order and keep the active action beside its explanation.

tablet.guidance: Pair a stage summary with evidence only when both remain independently readable.

desktop.guidance: Use the twelve column route for alternating chapters, a working region, and compact context.

zoom.guidance: Let stage labels, actions, and evidence wrap without clipping or overlap.

reflow.guidance: Convert the route to one vertical sequence while retaining every status and action.

subtle.usage: Stage markers, badges, and restrained detail.

control.usage: Buttons, fields, menu items, and compact interactive surfaces.

panel.usage: Cards, process bands, dialogs, and evidence panels.

hairline.usage: Internal routes, dividers, and table structure.

strong.usage: Focus, active stages, and consequential separation.

flat.usage: Default surfaces separated by boundaries and spacing.

raised.usage: Movable queue items and temporary emphasis.

overlay.usage: Dialogs, menus, and temporary content above the route.

buttons.guidance: Use one filled primary cue per decision region and keep secondary actions bounded but quiet.

states.default: Use the primary cue with a stable result focused label.
states.hover: Deepen the cue without changing size or position.
states.focus: Show the semantic focus ring outside the control boundary.
states.active: Move by at most one pixel and preserve nearby layout.
states.disabled: Keep the action readable and expose the missing prerequisite.
states.loading: Retain the action label beside a visible progress indicator.
states.success: Name the completed result with text and the success role.
states.error: Name the failed operation and its recovery using the destructive role.

links.guidance: Use specific destinations, persistent underlines, and the primary cue only for actionable text.

states.default: Underline the destination and use the accessible primary role.
states.hover: Strengthen the underline without changing line height.
states.focus: Frame the link with the same semantic focus ring as controls.
states.active: Retain the destination while showing immediate activation.
states.disabled: Render unavailable destinations as explained text instead of links.
states.loading: Keep the destination label and add adjacent busy status.
states.success: Confirm the local navigation result in nearby text.
states.error: Explain the local failure without relying on color.

forms.guidance: Group fields by outcome, keep help persistent, and place validation in the same reading path.
forms.help: Updates go to this address when ownership or stage changes.

inputs.textareaPlaceholder: Add the context the next owner needs.
inputs.guidance: Align fields to the route, keep labels visible, and reserve stable space for help and validation.

cards.title: Review window
cards.description: The active handoff keeps owner, due time, scope, and next action together.
cards.guidance: Use one card for one handoff and attach compact evidence to the decision it supports.

panels.title: Route summary
panels.description: The process panel keeps completed, current, and upcoming work visible in one bounded region.
panels.guidance: Use internal rules and stage labels instead of nesting separate cards for each route item.

navigation.label: Workflow stages
navigation.guidance: Name the current stage in text, preserve sequence, and keep every destination reachable by keyboard.

dataDisplay.guidance: Keep stage, ownership, freshness, and action context aligned with each work item.
dataDisplay.overflowGuidance: Preserve the complete comparison in a labelled keyboard reachable scroll region when priority columns cannot fit.

badges.label: Waiting
badges.meaning: The route has not reached this stage

badges.label: Current
badges.meaning: This stage owns the next valid action

badges.label: Complete
badges.meaning: The stage finished with a verified result

alerts.title: Route ready to continue
alerts.description: Every required review has a verified result.

alerts.title: Owner response required
alerts.description: Resolve the missing approval before the route can continue.

states.loading: Preparing the current route without hiding completed work…
states.empty: This route has no work items yet.
states.filteredEmpty: No work items match the active stage and owner filters.
states.error: The route could not refresh. Existing work remains available.
states.success: The review is complete and the next stage is ready.
states.disabled: Publishing remains unavailable until every required review is complete.
states.destructive: Removing this route also removes its pending handoffs.

feedback.guidance: Attach state to the affected work item, preserve existing evidence, and include the next useful recovery.
feedback.nonColorGuidance: Pair every status color with a label, icon, boundary, or stage position.

dialogs.title: Confirm route handoff
dialogs.description: Review the next owner, due time, and included work before continuing.
dialogs.guidance: Keep the handoff summary concise, place safe review first, and preserve the originating context.
dialogs.escapeBehavior: Escape closes the dialog because the handoff is not applied until confirmation.
dialogs.focusRestoration: Return focus to the handoff control that opened the dialog.

destructiveActions.consequence: Pending stages and their unsubmitted handoff context will be removed.
destructiveActions.recoverability: This preview action is reversible and changes only local specimen state.
destructiveActions.guidance: Repeat the route name, consequence, and real recovery status before the destructive boundary.

motion.guidance: Move attention along the route with short axis aligned transitions and no ambient or continuous motion.

reducedMotion.guidance: Remove translation, scaling, smooth scrolling, and loops while preserving immediate labelled route changes.

accessibility.semantics: Use native landmarks, headings, controls, tables, lists, and status regions before adding ARIA.
accessibility.keyboard: Keep route navigation, stage actions, overflow regions, menus, and dialogs fully operable in logical source order.
accessibility.focus: Use a persistent two pixel focus indicator and restore focus after every modal interaction.
accessibility.contrast: Measure text, controls, boundaries, status, and focus in both supported color schemes.
accessibility.targetSize: Provide targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels with adequate spacing and prefer 44 pixels for primary touch actions.
accessibility.zoom: Preserve every status, label, and action at 200 percent page zoom and 400 percent browser zoom.
accessibility.reflow: Reflow the route to 320 CSS pixels without two dimensional page scrolling.
accessibility.forcedColors: Retain boundaries, active stage, focus, selection, and feedback when system colors replace authored colors.
accessibility.statusCommunication: Announce async outcomes intentionally and never rely on color, position, or motion alone.

productSurfaces.guidance: These specimens demonstrate Relay structure only. Replace illustrative words with supplied Project language and preserve every real workflow rule.

marketing.title: Outcome and evidence route
marketing.description: A concise outcome opens into sequential chapters with credible working evidence.
elements: Alternating outcome and product evidence bands

authentication.title: Focused workspace entry
authentication.description: A bounded form keeps recovery, trust context, and pending feedback visible.

onboarding.title: Visible setup route
onboarding.description: The sequence keeps completed, current, optional, and upcoming work understandable together.
elements: Skippable optional work and verification states

dashboard.title: Work in motion
dashboard.description: Current work, blocked items, and the next valid decision lead the overview.

table.title: Routed work comparison
table.description: Work item, stage, owner, freshness, and actions remain aligned.

form.title: Outcome grouped input
form.description: Fields, validation, save state, and consequences stay attached to one outcome.
elements: Dirty, saving, saved, conflict, and failed feedback

settings.title: Scoped controls
settings.description: Personal, workspace, and organization settings explain their reach before action.

states.title: Stable route feedback
states.description: Loading, empty, error, success, disabled, and destructive states retain working context.
elements: Visible state name and affected object

evidencePresentation.preview: The Design System Preview is a public visual and descriptive specimen of evaluated direction.
evidencePresentation.designContract: The complete Design Contract is the public raw Markdown installed into a Project.
evidencePresentation.evaluation: Evaluation metadata and raw evidence paths remain public so coverage can be inspected.
